items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: His name was Mike Phillips. Mike and I were just — I mean we were just pals.

ctx.x: Did this group of students that you were included in, what was your reception like with your fellow white students?

You know young people are a lot more flexible than older people think sometimes. And of course there were some people that were aloof and strange and may have come from homes that taught them to have somewhat slanted maybe potentially racist viewpoints. But for the most part we were just kids. We just had a ball. The guy I was telling you about that I got this bass from, this tin bass, he was a white kid. We were buddies. We didn’t think about it. His name was Mike Phillips. Mike and I were just — I mean we were…

cultural things that are different. But we can coexist. I can appreciate you. I mean I don’t look at you and say oh yeah Monk is a white guy. You are just a friend. You’re just a guy that I like and we have — there’s a chemistry between us, and the vibes between us, there’s nothing hostile about what we are feeling. I don’t have any predetermined opinions about who and what you are. I come together to dialogue with you. See people spend too much time talking at or to. They don’t dialogue with. It’s not about…
